title: US-China AI Dialogue Launches Amid Trump Visit to Shenzhen
summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent announces new US-China AI cooperation framework ahead of Trump's APEC visit, including model testing standards and incident alerts.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- US Treasury Secretary announces new AI cooperation framework with China featuring direct incident alert channels and shared model testing standards.
- Dialogue established ahead of Trump's fourth meeting with Xi Jinping in 2026, focusing on preventing misunderstandings between competing AI systems.
- Both nations commit to exchanging best practices for evaluating advanced AI models before release while maintaining human oversight of the technology.


The United States and China have established a formal artificial intelligence dialogue framework designed to prevent misunderstandings and manage shared risks between the world's two largest economies. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the initiative November 11, 2026, highlighting unprecedented engagement between American and Chinese leaders on AI governance ahead of President Donald Trump's visit to Shenzhen for the APEC summit next week.


## Official Launch and Framework


Officially launched on November 11, 2026, the bilateral AI dialogue represents a significant diplomatic development in technology cooperation. Speaking to the National Committee on US-China Relations in New York, Bessent outlined that Trump and Xi Jinping have "established a new dialogue" on what the president terms "super intelligence." The framework includes direct channels for promptly alerting each nation of serious incidents involving AI models, a mechanism designed to prevent escalation of technical issues into diplomatic crises.


Chinese Ambassador Xie Feng reinforced the importance of the partnership, stating that "joint efforts of China and the United States are indispensable" for advancing AI governance globally. The cooperation extends beyond incident response to include exchanging best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release to ensure human judgment remains firmly in command of AI technology.


## Model Testing and Safety Standards


The dialogue establishes shared protocols for pre-release evaluation of advanced AI systems, addressing growing concerns about the safety and alignment of increasingly capable models. Both nations have committed to exchanging methodologies for testing AI systems before deployment, though specific technical standards remain under negotiation. The framework emphasizes maintaining human oversight and preventing autonomous AI decision-making in critical applications.


This cooperation arrives amid heightened scrutiny of AI development practices in both countries. The United States has raised concerns about[Chinese AI firms' safety standards](https://emergent.sh/news/china-imposes-new-safety-standards-ai-firms) , while China has implemented new regulatory frameworks for domestic AI companies. The bilateral dialogue aims to bridge these different regulatory approaches while establishing minimum shared safeguards.


## Economic and Strategic Context


Bessent's announcement comes as the world's two largest economies extend their tariff truce until January 2027, though significant trade tensions persist. The Treasury Secretary reiterated the administration's position of seeking to "de-risk, not to decouple" from China, calling for a "big, beautiful rebalancing" in economic ties. Recent consultations between Bessent and Vice Premier He Lifeng in September laid groundwork for the AI dialogue alongside broader economic discussions.


The timing of the announcement precedes Trump's third visit to China in 2026, where he will meet Xi for their fourth bilateral meeting this year. The frequency of leader-level engagement marks a departure from previous years, with Bessent noting that "never before have our leaders engaged face-to-face so often in a single year." Trump and Xi are scheduled to meet again in Miami at the G20 summit later in 2026.


## Implementation and Future Cooperation


The dialogue operates through existing economic consultation mechanisms established by Bessent and Vice Premier He, including the Boards of Trade and Investment created to manage bilateral economic relationships. Ambassador Xie emphasized the importance of leveraging both political-diplomatic channels and economic-trade consultation mechanisms to implement the AI cooperation framework effectively.


Specific implementation details include quarterly technical exchanges, joint research initiatives on AI safety, and coordination on international AI governance standards. Both nations have committed to transparent reporting of significant AI incidents through the direct alert channel, though the threshold for what constitutes a reportable incident remains subject to bilateral negotiation.


## What This Means


The establishment of formal US-China AI cooperation channels represents a pragmatic approach to managing technological competition between rival superpowers. By creating mechanisms for incident alerts and shared testing standards, both nations acknowledge that uncoordinated AI development poses risks that transcend national boundaries. The framework's success will depend on implementation details and whether technical cooperation can survive broader geopolitical tensions. For the global AI industry, the dialogue signals that even competing nations recognize the necessity of coordination on safety standards and risk management for increasingly powerful AI systems.
